Definition: grain of any kind (even while standing in the field); by extension the open country
BiblicalUsage: Bar is grain, the corn of the field, gathered and stored and sold. Joseph gathers it in Egypt until it cannot be measured, his brothers go down to buy it in the famine, Amos rebukes the merchants who cannot wait for the sabbath to end so they can sell it, and Proverbs says the people curse the man who withholds it and bless the man who sells it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe grain in Scripture is always about trust, because it is the difference between eating and starving. Joseph stored it by God's wisdom, the merchants sold it by greed, and I hold that what a man does with his grain shows what he believes about God.
